# vitest-auto-spy

> Auto-generate fully-typed test spies from a class, a type or nothing at all — one API across
> Vitest, `bun test` and `node:test`, plus Angular/NestJS/React/Vue/Svelte adapters. A drop-in
> successor to `jest-auto-spies`. Zero runtime dependencies.

- Install: `npm i -D vitest-auto-spy`
- Repository: https://github.com/ASDAlexey/vitest-auto-spy
- Documentation: https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/
- Offline agent cheat sheet, shipped inside the package: `node_modules/vitest-auto-spy/AGENTS.md`
- Everything below inlined as one file: https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/llms-full.txt

The one-line orientation: `createSpyFromClass(Class)` when a class exists, `createAutoMock<T>()`
when only a type does, `createMock<T>(partial)` when the double is read rather than called. Each
spied method earns helpers from its return type — `calledWith`/`mustBeCalledWith` always,
`resolveWith`/`rejectWith` for a `Promise`, `nextWith`/`throwWith` for an `Observable`.

## Core

- [Getting started](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/introduction): Install vitest-auto-spy and write your first Angular spec with a typed spy of a whole service, on Vitest.
- [Installation](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/installation): Install vitest-auto-spy, check what your project needs, and wire it into Angular CLI, Vitest, Bun, node:test or Rstest.
- [Compatibility](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/compatibility): Why each minimum version is what it is, which module formats ship, and how CI checks the oldest supported versions.
- [How it works](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/how-it-works): The two ideas behind vitest-auto-spy - reading a class's methods at run time, and types that pick each method's helpers from its return type.
- [createSpyFromClass](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/create-spy-from-class): Build a typed Spy<T> from a class - every method becomes a spy; options, accessor spies, spying on a real object, and edge cases.
- [returns vs overrides](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/returns-vs-overrides): Two options that set a spy's values when you create it; returns sets what a method answers, overrides replaces a member with a plain value.
- [Control helpers](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/control-helpers): calledWith, mustBeCalledWith, resolveWith, nextWith and the rest - the helpers that tell a spied method what to answer, picked by its return type.
- [Auto-mock by type](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/auto-mock-by-type): createAutoMock, mockDeep and createMock - build a spy or a test object from a TypeScript type or interface, with no class at runtime.
- [Strict mode](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/strict-mode): strict and onUnstubbedCall - a spy method nobody configured throws and names the class, the method and the arguments, instead of returning undefined.
- [Observable assertions](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/observable-assertions): expectEmission, expectEmissions, expectNoEmission, expectCompletion and expectError - assertions on a stream that fail when the stream stays silent.
- [Bridging Spy<T> and T](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/spy-typing): Why Spy<T> is not assignable to T, the two helpers asInstance and asSpy that convert between them without a cast, and how to read the TypeScript errors spies produce.
- [Performance](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/core/performance): What each factory costs, which settings make a slow or memory-hungry suite faster, and the measurements behind each claim.

## Spec patterns

- [Patterns that hold up](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/recipes): Short recipes for everyday Angular specs - replacing a service in TestBed, setting signals and Observables, effects, timers, network, console and test data.
- [Mocking classes](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/guides/mocking-classes): Replace a class in a Vitest spec - createSpyFromClass compared with vi.spyOn on the prototype and a vi.mock factory, arrow-function fields, and classes the code under test creates with new.
- [Mocking localStorage](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/guides/mocking-local-storage): Replace localStorage or sessionStorage for one test with stubWebStorage - fill it, check what was stored, and get it restored automatically; when a spy on setItem or another approach fits better.
- [Mocking Prisma Client](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/guides/mocking-prisma): A typed PrismaClient mock from mockDeep - answer findMany and create with resolveWith, rejectWith, resolveWithPerCall and calledWith, reset between tests with resetAutoSpy, and run an interactive $transaction against the same mock.
- [Storybook stories (Angular)](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/guides/storybook-angular): Run Angular stories as Vitest tests with the Storybook Vitest addon, hand the component auto-spied services through applicationConfig and provideAutoSpy, configure them in beforeEach and assert on them in play.
- [Angular Material idioms](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/guides/angular-material-idioms): The literal doubles Angular Material's own specs hand-write — a ScrollStrategy, MAT_ICON_LOCATION, MATERIAL_ANIMATIONS, ScrollDispatcher — rewritten with createAutoMock, provideAutoSpyForToken and provideAutoSpy, plus a partial double of a real service.
- [Testing without the DOM](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/guides/testing-without-the-dom): Write Angular component specs that never read markup - assert on signals, outputs and spies, render with renderShallow, and enforce it with the templates 'never' lint option.
- [Angular unit-test builder](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/guides/angular-unit-test-builder): Run specs that use vitest-auto-spy under ng test and the @angular/build unit-test builder - setup files, vi.mock rules, coverage, shards and code splitting.

## Runtimes

- [Vitest](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/runtimes/vitest): Use vitest-auto-spy on Vitest with no configuration, add an optional setup file, and handle Vitest 5, isolate false, sharding and browser mode.
- [Bun](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/runtimes/bun): Use vitest-auto-spy with Bun's bun:test - a runnable example, what differs from Vitest, cleanup between tests and Bun 1.4 runner flags.
- [Angular on Bun](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/runtimes/bun-angular): Run Angular TestBed specs under bun test with one preload line - a DOM, inlined templates and a zoneless TestBed.
- [node:test](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/runtimes/node): Use vitest-auto-spy with Node's built-in test runner - a runnable example, where node:test mocks differ, spy names and freeing mock memory.
- [Rstest](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/runtimes/rstest): Use vitest-auto-spy with Rstest, the Rspack-based test runner - a runnable example, how its mocks compare to Vitest and what is not supported yet.
- [RxJS](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/runtimes/rxjs): Make a spied method or property return an Observable you control - nextWith, nextWithValues, nextWithPerCall, returnSubject, delays and resets.

## Utilities

- [Explaining a double](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/explain-spy): Print what a spy is configured to answer next to what it was actually called with, before anything has failed. Lives on the /diagnostics entry.
- [Console spies](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/console): Silent, typed spies over the global console from vitest-auto-spy/console - install them for the tests that expect output, assert on them, and they come off after each test.
- [Call log](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/call-log): createLog is one journal every collaborator writes to, so a spec can assert the order of calls across several objects as a single value.
- [Test-run hygiene](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/setup): setupAutoSpy() in your Vitest setup file puts back what a test leaves behind - patched properties, timers, listeners, globals - and names the test that left it.
- [Fake timers](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/fake-timers): setupFakeTimers installs fake timers for a describe and removes them after each test; advanceTimers moves the clock and waits for the promises the timers started.
- [Observer stubs](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/observer-stubs): stubIntersectionObserver and friends replace an observer the component creates itself with one the spec drives, and put the real global back after the test.
- [Constructor doubles](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/constructor-doubles): mockConstructor and stubConstructor build a stand-in the code under test can call with new, which a vi.fn() with an arrow function cannot be.
- [Media element stub](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/media-element): stubMediaElement makes video and audio elements play, report a duration and fire the events a component listens for, which jsdom does not do.
- [Worker stub](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/worker-stub): stubWorker replaces the Worker your code creates with one whose replies come from the spec, and puts the real global back after the test.
- [Frames and element boxes](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/frame-and-rect): stubAnimationFrame runs requestAnimationFrame when the spec says, and stubElementRect makes getBoundingClientRect report a box; both are put back after the test.
- [Element stub and missing DOM APIs](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/element-stub): createElementStub gives an HTMLElement for ElementRef whose spies keep state, and fillMissingDomApis fills the members jsdom and happy-dom leave out, once, from the setup file.
- [Module mocks](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/module-mocks): assertMocked proves a vi.mock() applied, moduleNamespace gives a mock factory the shape libraries expect, and adoptMock adds calledWith and resolveWith to the mocks it built.
- [Tracking injections](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/track-injections): trackInjections records which dependencies your code actually asked DI for, and gives each one an auto-spy. Works with Angular and NestJS.
- [Fixtures without casts](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/fixtures): createMock takes a deep partial, createFixture and createFixtureFactory build a model many specs share, narrow() picks the branch of a union a test knows it got, and withOverrides() keeps a model's getters.
- [fakeAsync on Vitest](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/zone): vitest-auto-spy/zone makes Angular's fakeAsync and waitForAsync work on Vitest. A separate import, so a zoneless project never loads it.
- [Waiting and the clock](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/event-loop): flushEventLoop, flushEventLoopUntil and settleDynamicImport wait for work a promise cannot; mockSystemTime and useCountingClock control what Date says.
- [ESLint plugin](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/eslint-plugin): Fifty-seven lint rules for spec files. They catch tests that pass without checking anything, doubles that drift from the real class, and setup that leaks between tests. Flat config, part of the package.
- [ESLint rules](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/eslint-rules): One section per rule of the ESLint plugin - what it reports, a before and after example, its options, how to fix a report and when to turn the rule off.
- [CLI — doctor, perf & init](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/cli): npx vitest-auto-spy is a command line tool that ships with the package. doctor finds test-setup mistakes that never fail a run, perf shows where test time goes and can fail CI over a slow test, init points coding agents at the library, and ng-test adds shards and changed-only runs to the Angular builder.
- [CLI — the codemod](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/codemod): Migrate a test suite off jest-auto-spies and Jest, or off jasmine-auto-spies and jasmine. The codemod rewrites what it can decide safely, leaves the rest as it was, and lists every place left for you. It previews by default, writes with --write, and --verify fails CI when leftovers come back.
- [Editor diagnostics](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/utilities/editor-diagnostics): See the vitest-auto-spy lint rules underlined while you write a spec, in WebStorm and other JetBrains IDEs, and through the ESLint extension in VS Code, Cursor and Windsurf.

## Adapters

- [Angular](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/angular): Test Angular components and services in TestBed with spies built from the real classes - provideAutoSpy, injectSpy, renderShallow, stable, signal and resource helpers.
- [Angular HTTP](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/angular-http): Answer httpResource() and HttpClient requests in an Angular test with one line - provideHttpTesting, expectRequest and a check for requests nobody answered.
- [Angular router](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/angular-router): Test stand-ins for ActivatedRoute, Router and Location. Set route params, move the URL, assert navigate() and check where the app went, without a real router.
- [Signal forms](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/signal-forms): createForm builds an Angular signal form inside a test without the NG0203 injection error; toHaveFieldErrors checks a field's validation errors in one line.
- [Angular diagnostics](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/angular-diagnostics): enableAngularDiagnostics turns five silent mistakes in Angular specs into failing tests - dead NgModule imports, dead schemas, real services where a spy was expected, unanswered HTTP requests and spies the component's own providers hide.
- [Component provider overrides](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/angular-overrides): overrideComponentProvider and overrideAutoSpy — replace a dependency a component declares for itself, and get told when the override did not apply.
- [Angular troubleshooting](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/angular-troubleshooting): Errors an Angular spec can hit before your own code runs - two copies of Angular testing, an already created testing module, NG0101, empty NgModule scopes, broken component definitions.
- [How the Angular helpers work](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/angular-how-it-works): Why the Angular entry points, stand-ins, matchers and checks behave as they do - the Angular and builder details behind each rule.
- [NestJS](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/nestjs): Replace a service's dependencies with typed spies in Test.createTestingModule, or build the service with createNestUnit and no testing module at all.
- [React](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/react): Spy the classes a React app owns (services, stores, API clients) and pass the spy to a Context provider or a hook; mock a custom hook with a typed return value.
- [Vue / Pinia](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/vue): provideAutoSpy builds a global.provide map for @vue/test-utils, and createSpyFromClass spies a class-based Pinia store.
- [Svelte](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/adapters/svelte): Spy class-based Svelte services and stores, and pass the spy to the component through props, context or a mocked module.

## Upgrading

- [To 5.0 — the Angular and rxjs peer floors](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/upgrading-5): Two breaking changes, both peer ranges. Angular moves to >=20 and gains @angular/platform-browser; rxjs moves to >=7.2 because the deep operator path is gone in rxjs 8. What to change, and what stays.
- [To 4.0 — rxjs out of your program](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/upgrading-4): Three breaking changes; rxjs leaves the published declarations, the DOM stubs and run diagnostics get their own subpaths, and every lint rule becomes an error. What to change, and what stays.
- [To 3.0 — the vitest peer range](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/upgrading-3): One change - the vitest peer range is now >=2.1.0. No shipped code changed; dist size, runtime and memory are the same as 2.0.
- [To 2.0 — additive methodsToSpyOn, lazy spies](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/upgrading-2): What to change when you move from 1.x to 2.0 - usually nothing, one rename at most. methodsToSpyOn now adds spies instead of removing them, and method spies are created lazily.
- [Migrating from jest-auto-spies](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/migrating): A step-by-step swap from jest-auto-spies or @bugsplat/vitest-auto-spies, plus the per-runner gotchas.
- [Migrating from jasmine-auto-spies](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/migrating-jasmine): Move a Jasmine or Karma test project that uses jasmine-auto-spies to Vitest. Swap one import so the specs run unchanged, then let the codemod rewrite them, with mapping tables for the auto-spies API and the jasmine globals.
- [Migrating from @ngneat/spectator](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/migrating-spectator): Move Spectator service and component specs to vitest-auto-spy - the API side by side, full before and after specs, the DOM parts you keep, and why Spectator fails on Angular 22.
- [Migrating from Suites](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/migrating-suites): A spec-by-spec translation from TestBed.solitary and TestBed.sociable to createNestUnit — the API shapes side by side, what each side refuses, and what the move costs.
- [Migrating from @testing-library/angular](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/migrating-testing-library-angular): Replace createMock and provideMock from @testing-library/angular/vitest-utils with vitest-auto-spy and keep render, screen and the queries - the mapping, a before and after spec, and the two defects it fixes.
- [After the refactor-jasmine-vitest schematic](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/migrating-angular-schematic): Angular's refactor-jasmine-vitest schematic turns jasmine.createSpyObj into hand-written vi.fn() literals and leaves three TODOs. createSpyFromClass closes all three in one line; this page shows the real output beside the fix.
- [API reference](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/api): Every export of vitest-auto-spy, grouped by import path, one line each, with a link to the page that documents it.
- [Glossary](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/glossary): The words these docs use, what each one means in a spec, and the Russian term the translation uses for it.
- [Comparison](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/comparison): How vitest-auto-spy compares to jest-auto-spies, vitest-mock-extended, @golevelup/ts-vitest, @suites/unit, ng-mocks, @testing-library/angular, spectator, sinon and Vitest's own built-ins, with last-release dates.
- [For AI agents](https://asdalexey.github.io/vitest-auto-spy/agents): llms.txt, llms-full.txt, a bundled AGENTS.md and a Claude Code skill — how to point Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any other agent at this library.
